source_text: Has vires exseramus in traducem, dicamusque: Si Christus, qui homo factus est, non habuit naturale peccatum, quomodo dicunt quidam in vobis quia imagini Dei pravitas dominetur ingenita? Si autem in natura malum est, et Christus, qui in eadem natura deprehenditur, sub regno diaboli est constitutus. Si autem ille creditur reus, inanis est praedicatio nostra, et vacua est fides vestra; inveniuntur autem falsi testes Apostoli, quia testimonium dixerunt adversus Deum, quod Filium suum, ex semine David secundum carnem, innocuum sanctumque formaverit, si eum maledicti seminis crimen infecit. Prorsus si in tali Christo speramus, miserabiliores sumus omnibus hominibus. Nunc autem Christus non minus verus homo, quam verus Deus, de Adam stirpe generatus, factus ex muliere, factusque sub lege, nullum fecit, et ideo nullum habuit peccatum. Apparet igitur crimen voluntatis esse, non seminis.
pass_a_gloss: Let us put forth these powers into the tradux, and let us say: If Christ, who was made a human, did not have a natural sin, how do certain people say among you that an inborn crookedness lords it over the image of God? But if there is evil in nature, even Christ, who is caught in the same nature, is established under the devil's kingdom. But if he is believed guilty, our preaching is empty, and your faith is vacant; but the Apostles are found false witnesses, because they said testimony against God, that he formed his Son, from the seed of David according to the flesh, innocent and holy, if the charge of a cursed seed infected him. Indeed if we hope in such a Christ, we are more miserable than all humans. But now Christ no less a true human than true God, generated from Adam's stock, made from a woman, and made under the law, did none, and therefore had no sin. It appears therefore that a charge is of will, not of seed.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: Let us turn this force against inherited sin and say: If Christ, who became human, had no natural sin, how do some among you say inborn depravity rules God’s image? If evil exists in nature, Christ too, found in that same nature, is placed under the devil’s kingdom. If he is believed guilty, our preaching is empty and your faith is empty. The apostles are found false witnesses, because they testified against God that he formed his Son innocent and holy, from David’s seed according to the flesh (Romans 1:3), if the crime of cursed seed infected him. Certainly, if we hope in such a Christ, we are more pitiable than all people (compare 1 Corinthians 15:12–19).

But now Christ, no less truly human than truly God, generated from Adam’s stock, made from a woman and made under the law (Galatians 4:4), committed no sin and therefore had no sin (1 Peter 2:22). It is therefore clear that guilt belongs to will, not reproductive seed (1 Corinthians 15:12–19) (Genesis 1:26–27).

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
